title: Cloudflare acquires Node.js creator’s startup that copied its serverless playbook
key_facts: Cloudflare announced on Friday (9 Oct) that the entire Deno team is joining it; Deno was co-founded by Node.js creator Ryan Dahl.
Deno's standalone runtime and cloud hosting service will be wound down; the team will work on Cloudflare Workers.
The Deno runtime gets monthly maintenance and security updates for another year; Deno Deploy shuts in six months with migration help; the JSR registry continues under Cloudflare.
Deno raised around $26 million across two rounds.

In August Deno released Celld, an open-source recreation of Cloudflare's Workers and Durable Objects model; Cloudflare plans to merge it with its open-source runtime Workerd, led by Dahl and Bert Belder.
Cloudflare's Kenton Varda wrote that Cloudflare had not done a great job making its open-source runtime work outside its own network.
Dahl says the combined project should stay open source, likely under Apache 2.0, and highlights AI agents as an important use.
The article gives no purchase price.
quote_evidence: Cloudflare is buying the startup co-founded by Node.js creator Ryan Dahl, a longtime competitor that recently built its own open-source version of Cloudflare’s serverless computing platform.
The Deno runtime will receive monthly maintenance and security updates for another year, while Deno Deploy will shut down in six months, with migration assistance for paying customers.
why_it_matters_hint: A rival that copied Cloudflare's model joins it; Deno's own runtime and hosting are being retired.
notes: Announced jointly by Cloudflare and Deno in blog posts. No price given. Open-source promises are statements of intent.
